eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart donors using a non‑linear machine learning algorithm (k‑means clustering) and reports recipient survival outcomes, meeting all inclusion criteria for population, intervention, outcome, and study characteristics.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: National Institutes of Health (NIH)/National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute
identification_methods.Setting: Multicenter prospective observational cohort across organ procurement organizations in the United States
identification_methods.Comments: Prospective multicenter cohort study of potential heart donors after brain death
identification_methods.Institution: Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Medical Center; Stanford University School of Medicine
identification_methods.Address: 2238 Geary Boulevard, San Francisco, California 94115, USA
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Adult donors aged 18‑65 years after brain death, HIV negative, enrolled in the Donor Heart Study
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Unsupervised k‑means clustering (combined with supervised reclassification)
identification_methods.Input Variables: Wall motion scores for 17 myocardial segments, donor demographics, biomarkers (troponin‑I, NT‑proBNP), hemodynamics, medications
identification_methods.Validation Method: Optimal number of clusters selected by maximizing cubic clustering criterion; no external validation reported
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Core TTE interpretation blinded to clinical data; k‑means clustering followed by consolidation into four phenotypes based on clinical plausibility

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult donors (18-65 years) after brain death, HIV negative
population.Exclusion criteria: Donors not considered for cardiac donation (coroner restriction, known preexisting cardiac disease)
population.Target Population: Potential heart donors after brain death
population.Population Notes: Final analytical cohort included 913 initial TTEs with complete pre- and post-transplantation data

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Transthoracic echocardiogram wall motion scores (17 segment WMS)
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Baseline (initial TTE) and follow‑up TTE ~24 ± 6 h later
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Unsupervised k‑means clustering applied to donors with any RWMA, followed by reclassification based on clinical plausibility
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Donor heart acceptance for transplantation, recipient 2‑year survival
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary focus on donor heart acceptance rates across RWMA phenotypes; recipient survival compared but no difference found
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Focal basal septal (FBS) phenotype had highest acceptance (68%); no significant difference in 2‑year recipient survival among phenotypes
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reporting: 68% acceptance for FBS phenotype; overall acceptance 54.5%
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Proportion of donor hearts accepted for transplantation among each RWMA phenotype
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: No significant differences in recipient 2‑year survival across phenotypes despite acceptance variation
